judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the screen-only label 'E-mail' (for=form-field-email) of the footer newsletter form. The page has two inputs with id=form-field-email, so this label resolves to the first one in the lead form, whose name becomes 'E-mail E-mail'. The claim is true of the capture, and the live HTML has the same duplicate. But 4.1.2 asks that the control have a programmatically determinable name. The footer field still has one: Chrome computes 'Digite seu e-mail' from its placeholder, and the ACT rule e086e5 (mapped to 4.1.2) accepts a placeholder as the accessible name (Passed Example 5). The lead-form field's doubled name 'E-mail E-mail' is redundant but still accurate. The duplicate id is a 4.1.1 parsing matter, which WCAG 2.1's note treats as always satisfied for HTML. So no control fails 4.1.2 here: the rule treats the broken reference itself as the failure, a stricter rule than the criterion's.
